payload.title: settleClaim's revision-CAS check has no reconcile path, refuses return for any claimed item edited…
payload.description:
settleClaim's revision-CAS check has no reconcile path, refuses return for any claimed item edited mid-lifecycle

Kind: bug (correctness/blocking — affects the driving loop's own core capability)
Risk: heavy (claim/coordination core, blocks item completion)

## Problem

docs/architect/doing-coordination-redesign.md §16.3 (Required Tests, Settle) requires: "Settlement after durable revision drift fails or goes through explicit reconcile." Only the fail branch exists — settleClaim (src/state/store.mjs:1101-1105) throws StoreError('conflict', ...) unconditionally on any preClaimRevision mismatch, with no reconcile parameter/flag/path anywhere in settleClaim, fgos return, or fgos catchup.

getItemDurableRevision (src/state/runtime-coordination.mjs:49-53) hashes the item's ENTIRE JSON at claim time (fgos pick/take) and compares it again at settle time (fgos return). Any fgos edit / fgos discover / fgos plan / fgos gate-approve call on the item between claim and settle changes this hash — even from the SAME session/actor doing its own legitimate, expected work, not a concurrent conflict. fgos-coding-planning and fgos-coding-discovering both routinely call fgos edit mid-lifecycle on a claimed item by design (syncing tier/kind/risk/docsRef/verify/action/footprint), so this looks reproducible on any coding-domain item driven discovery->planning->executing->return under one continuous claim -- the exact flow tsk-40m's own redesign intentionally kept as ONE unbroken claim (releaseClaimOnExecuting retired to a no-op specifically so a runtime claim stays active straight through clarify->executing).

## Live repro (tsk-1sl, 2026-08-26)

1. fgos pick tsk-1sl -> claim clm-1787728460694-0940b99e, preClaimRevision 3db05e6a67e4d38c (captured at claim time).
2. Normal discovery+planning stage-skill calls: fgos edit (tier/kind/risk), fgos edit (docsRef), fgos discover --verdict clear, fgos edit (verify/action/footprint), fgos gate-approve, fgos plan --verdict pass-through -- all routine, all through the one door.
3. fgos return tsk-1sl -> refuses: settleClaim: item "tsk-1sl" durable revision changed from "3db05e6a67e4d38c" to "177d8fd5c05d7df8". Exit 3. Claim survives untouched (confirmed via .fgos/runtime/claims/tsk-1sl.json -- same claimId, same stale preClaimRevision).

## Acceptance criteria

- settleClaim (or a caller) implements the doc's own "or goes through explicit reconcile" branch for a revision drift caused by the SAME claim-holder's own legitimate durable writes (never for a genuinely different actor's conflicting edit -- that case should keep refusing).
- A real end-to-end coding-domain item (discovery -> planning with at least one fgos edit -> executing -> return) completes without a CAS conflict, proven live, not just unit-tested.
- Existing CAS-conflict-must-refuse tests (test/state/runtime-coordination.test.mjs) still pass for a genuine concurrent-actor conflict.

## Verify

Reproduce tsk-1sl's own sequence above end to end (claim -> edit -> discover -> plan -> return) against the fix and confirm return succeeds; then run test/state/runtime-coordination.test.mjs to confirm the existing conflict-refusal tests for a real concurrent conflict still pass.

## Footprint

src/state/store.mjs, src/state/runtime-coordination.mjs, possibly bin/fgos.mjs (return/catchup)
